retellLiveKitProtocol.verdict: Technically workable, not yet confirmed by Retell. The official browser SDK's LiveKit path is a thin wrapper over livekit-client: it joins Retell's LiveKit room with the minted access_token and nothing else, publishes the microphone, plays the remote track 'agent_audio', and reads JSON data packets from the participant 'server'. livekit-client runs in React Native through @livekit/react-native (registerGlobals supplies WebRTC), so the phone can speak the same protocol natively. Open risks: Retell's support statement (US-020 AC1), the 'gateway' transport Retell added in SDK 3.0.0 (Sep 2026: WHIP-style signalling, not LiveKit) if Retell moves web calls to it, and the v3 note that calls made by /v3/create-web-call send no talking/transcript events (our server mints with /v2/create-web-call).
retellLiveKitProtocol.mint: POST /api/voice/web-call {chat_id?} with the app's bearer + X-Workspace-ID → today {call_id, access_token, chat_id} (api/voice_retell.py:252-256); after W1 US-008a also transport?, url?, ice_servers?, expires_at? whenever Retell returns them. The server calls https://api.retellai.com/v2/create-web-call with the workspace's secret Retell key (modules/voice/retell_api.py); the phone never sees a Retell key. The access_token dies in about 30 s unused: join at once.
retellLiveKitProtocol.transportChoice: transport absent or 'livekit' → LiveKit. Absent means a LiveKit-only backend (retell-client-js-sdk 3.0.2 src/types.ts CreateWebCallResponse: 'Missing on older backends, which are LiveKit-only'; src/transport.ts selectTransport defaults to 'livekit'; the legacy RetellWebClient's defaultTransport is 'livekit'). transport 'gateway' (or anything else) → not LiveKit: refused honestly in v1 (KV16).
retellLiveKitProtocol.join: new Room({audioCaptureDefaults: {autoGainControl: true, echoCancellation: true, noiseSuppression: true, channelCount: 1}}); await room.connect(url ?? 'wss://retell-ai-4ihahnq7.livekit.cloud', access_token) — the token carries the room, no room name is passed; then room.localParticipant.setMicrophoneEnabled(true). Sources: 3.0.2 src/livekit-transport.ts:24 LIVEKIT_HOST and :41-112 connect(); 2.0.8 src/index.ts:15 hostUrl and startCall(). Nothing browser-specific is part of the join: no Origin, cookie or Retell key, only the URL and the token.
retellLiveKitProtocol.agentAudio: Retell's agent publishes an audio track whose publication.trackName is 'agent_audio'; its RoomEvent.TrackSubscribed is the 'call ready' signal (3.0.2 src/livekit-transport.ts:79-99). React Native plays a subscribed remote audio track by itself (the browser SDK's track.attach() is DOM-only).
retellLiveKitProtocol.dataPackets: RoomEvent.DataReceived(payload, participant): only from participant.identity === 'server'; payload = UTF-8 JSON (src/livekit-transport.ts:101-108). event_type 'update' {transcript: [{role 'agent' | 'user', content, metadata?}], turntaking?: 'agent_turn' | 'user_turn'} carries the WHOLE running transcript each time (replace, never append; the web takes the last utterance of each speaker: frontend/hooks/use-retell-call.ts); 'agent_start_talking' and 'agent_stop_talking' (no payload); 'metadata' {metadata}; 'node_transition'. The gateway's control envelope {type: 'status', state: 'ended' | 'replaced'} ends the call (src/session/base-session.ts handleDataEvent). Anything else is ignored (the SDK drops unknown events: src/session/events.ts DATA_CHANNEL_EVENTS).
retellLiveKitProtocol.eventsCaveat: retell-client-js-sdk 3.0.2 README 'Migrating from 2.x': 2.x calls emitted agent_start_talking, agent_stop_talking, update and metadata; calls created by the v3 createWebCall() (/v3/create-web-call) do not, and their transcript comes from Retell's monitor WebSocket, which carries an API key (never on a phone). automatos-ai mints with /v2/create-web-call, so the events flow today. Fallback the app builds anyway: speaking/listening from LiveKit's ActiveSpeakersChanged (a remote speaker = Auto speaking; the local participant = the user) and Auto's words from the thread (the server saves every turn and sends chat_changed).
retellLiveKitProtocol.leave: room.disconnect(). 'Leaving is what ends a web call; there is no one else to tell' (src/session/web-call-session.ts end()). The server's call-ended webhook stamps the call; the app makes no Retell call.
retellLiveKitProtocol.aiNotice: Inside Live the server speaks the AI greeting and the reminder itself (api/voice_retell.py _socket_ports → modules/voice/live_socket.py; modules/policy/ai_disclosure.py VOICE_GREETING / VOICE_REMINDER; modules/voice/ai_notice.py interval), so the app shows the AiLabel and speaks nothing extra.

'https://api.retellai.com'}/webrtc-proxy/{call_id}/v1/webrtc/sessions with 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>' and 'X-Retell-Client-JS-SDK-Version', body {identity: 'client', sdp: <offer>} → {session_id, sdp: <answer>}; trickle ICE as PATCH …/sessions/{session_id} {candidate}; DELETE …/sessions/{session_id} on close; ICE servers from the mint's ice_servers (the SDK's default stun:stun.l.google.com:19302); a data channel 'control' that Retell does not use yet (3.0.2 src/gateway-transport.ts). decisions.text: Retell has NOT confirmed (as of 21 Oct 2026) that a client other than its browser SDK may join a web call over LiveKit with the minted access_token (decision 32's first task; PRD-001 US-020 AC1). While value is false: no phase-2 story starts, no Live button exists, and quick-ask carries voice (PRD-001 §4.9). The lead flips value to true on the BRANCH's copy of this file (<worktree>/scripts/ralph/prd-001-voice.json; the runner never re-seeds a tracked kit json) in one signed '[skip ci]' commit whose body quotes Retell's answer, after recording it in PRD-001 US-020 (AC1). If Retell says no, or says web calls move to the gateway transport, value stays false and the lead decides between a gateway client (retellLiveKitProtocol.gatewayForTheRecord) and leaving Live out of v1. A build session NEVER edits this decision.

decisions.text: No WebView anywhere (Gerard: a WebView for voice 'sounds like a hack'). Quick-ask is expo-speech-recognition + expo-speech; Auto Live is LiveKit's React Native SDK. Nothing from Retell's browser SDK is loaded, embedded or imported.

Quick-ask for everyone, on every plan and edition, never gated: HOLD TO TALK, on-device speech recognition only (audio never goes to Apple or Google), the transcript sent through the normal chat with spokenMode, the reply spoken by the phone's text to speech; the client shows and speaks the AI notice once, at the start of a voice session; no ten-minute reminder (D73).

Auto Live joins Retell's call natively through LiveKit's React Native SDK with the mint's transport fields; full duplex with barge-in; the server speaks the AI greeting; receipts arrive in the thread over chat_changed. Business-only on SaaS (enforced at the mint, W1 US-008a); any armed self-hosted install; hidden until Retell confirms.
Hands-free means screen on, app open. No background microphone, no Android microphone foreground service. The mic never opens without a press; MIC LIVE is visible whenever it is open.

The HUD voice layout (A5's phone core) is the voice screen in every style, painted by that style's look: Studio ink and orange rings, Play's Ember rings with Auto in the centre, HUD its accent. Built on A5's components, never a copy.

The foundation's AiLabel ('Auto is an AI' / '{agent} is an AI') is one small muted caption (Body 6, the muted token) and sits on the voice screen, small and out of the way. Nothing is ever disabled on its visibility: there is no fence, and HOLD TO TALK, LIVE and typing never wait for it (useAiLabelVisible and AI_LABEL_PAUSED_TEXT no longer exist). (D73, Gerard 23 Oct: the AI label is one small muted caption, never a pill and never a lock; the voice notice is spoken once per session) src/styles/ai-label.tsx is never edited (gate-enforced).

Viewers get no voice: HOLD TO TALK disabled with 'Ask your workspace owner for editor access to talk to Auto' (src/auth/strings.ts) and no Live button; owners, admins and editors talk (roleCan 'chat').

No spoken_mode → quick-ask sends a plain turn and reads its plain text (the app strips markdown itself); no voice_live → no Live button (canSpokenMode, canVoiceLive from src/api/capabilities.ts). Gated on capabilities, never on a server version.
Nothing about plans, credits or prices: the Business-only refusal is never shown as written (W1's 403 'Auto Live is on the Business plan'); a workspace that cannot use Live never sees the button.
No pointer to creating an account anywhere on the voice screens ('Create an account', 'Sign up', 'No account?'). Gate-enforced on the wave's added lines.

No dependency, native module, config plugin or app.json change (package.json, package-lock.json, app.json and eas.json untouched — gate-enforced). Every module this wave uses is in the foundation's build (docs/native-modules.md 'Voice' rows).

All HTTP through the foundation's src/api client with this kit's route table src/voice/routes.ts (phase 2); zod at every boundary; unknown fields and unknown Retell packets ignored. Chat turns go through A2's controller only, never a second chat request.
Tokens only: colours come from the resolved style (A5's useStyle()); no colour literal outside src/styles/tokens/ (the lint rule).

Nothing under 11 pt; every animated signal (rings, waveform, cursor, the mascot) has a text twin (the chip, MIC LIVE, the transcript); Reduce Motion stops every loop; tap targets 44 pt; HOLD TO TALK works with a screen reader (KV5).

Files 200-400 lines (never over 800), functions under 50, components under 150, nesting under 4; pure logic in plain TS with vitest tests (pure modules import no react, react-native, expo-*, @livekit/* or livekit-client, so node can run them); immutability; copy in src/voice/strings.ts.

This kit may create or change ONLY: src/voice/**, app/(app)/voice.tsx, its own kit files under scripts/ralph/, and the NAMED seams of KV2. Never: src/core/**, src/api/**, src/auth/**, src/ui/**, src/navigation/** (this kit's app path lives in src/voice/nav.ts, KV17), src/storage/**, src/app-state/**, src/consent/** (read only), src/connect/**, src/cc/**, src/styles/** outside KV2's seams (and never src/styles/ai-label.tsx), src/chat/** outside KV2's seams, app/_layout.tsx, app/(app)/_layout.tsx, every other app route, any __tests__ folder of A2 or A5 (their tests pass unchanged), package.json, package-lock.json, app.json, eas.json, plugins/**, .github/**, scripts/* outside scripts/ralph/. Each story has a 'phase'. Phase 1 (US-019a..US-019k: quick-ask and the voice screen) needs A2 and A5 phase 1 in the base (needsInBase.phase1). Phase 2 (US-020a..US-020e: Auto Live) needs RETELL_LIVEKIT_CONFIRMED true in the branch's kit json AND the connect kit's src/consent/policy.ts in the branch: the gate's --print-phase prints 2 only then. A build session never starts a story above the current phase; when every story of the current phase is done it finishes the phase (gate, CI commit, RALPH_COMPLETE). Phase 2 is a second launch (after the lead flips the flag; with RALPH_BASE_MOVE=1 when the consent code must be merged in). In phase 1 nothing under src/voice/live/ exists and nothing imports @livekit/react-native or livekit-client (gate-enforced).
decisions.source: kit (lead brief: Live depends on an explicit RETELL_LIVEKIT_CONFIRMED line)

decisions.text: Speech recognition runs on the phone or not at all. iOS: start only when ExpoSpeechRecognitionModule.supportsOnDeviceRecognition() is true — the module sets requiresOnDeviceRecognition only when the recognizer supports it and otherwise silently uses Apple's servers (ios/ExpoSpeechRecognizer.swift:579-580), so the app checks first and never starts otherwise. Android: start only on API 33+ (the module creates SpeechRecognizer.createOnDeviceSpeechRecognizer only on TIRAMISU with requiresOnDeviceRecognition: ExpoSpeechService.kt:93-109; below 33 it falls through to SpeechRecognizer.createSpeechRecognizer, the phone's default recognition service, where EXTRA_PREFER_OFFLINE is only a preference and the audio may go to Google), with supportsOnDeviceRecognition() true and the language in getSupportedLocales({}).installedLocales (no service package: the on-device recognizer answers); a language that is supported but not installed offers androidTriggerOfflineModelDownload ('It stays on your phone'). Otherwise — Android 12 or older, no on-device recognizer, the language missing, an iPhone or language without on-device support — HOLD TO TALK is unavailable with a plain reason and typing stays; the app NEVER falls back to network recognition (the privacy policy says quick-ask speech stays on the phone: release-kit privacy audit, 21 Oct). Every start passes requiresOnDeviceRecognition: true; never androidRecognitionServicePackage (app.json's androidSpeechServicePackages only lists the Google app in <queries>); never recordingOptions.persist or audioSource (audio is never saved). The recognition language is the phone's first locale (expo-localization), the same one text to speech uses.
decisions.source: decision 32 ('forced on-device'), PRD-001 §4.9, lead brief ('on Android require on-device recognition where available and say what happens otherwise')

decisions.text: The mic opens only while HOLD TO TALK is held (press in → listen, release → send); a hold under HOLD_MIN_MS 300 is a tap ('Hold the button while you talk'), and listening stops itself at HOLD_MAX_MS 60 s. With a screen reader on (AccessibilityInfo.isScreenReaderEnabled) the button toggles instead (double-tap to talk, double-tap to send) and says so. Pressing while Auto speaks stops the speech at once (barge-in) and, if the turn still streams, cancels it on the server through A2's Stop. STOP aborts listening (nothing sent), stops speech and cancels a streaming turn. 'Auto, stop' (KV config STOP_PHRASES, whole utterance only) said during a hold acts as STOP and sends nothing. MIC LIVE follows the recognizer's audiostart/audioend events (the real capture), never the button state.

Only turns started by quick-ask are spoken, and only while the voice screen is mounted; a typed turn (TYPE) is never spoken. Spoken: Auto's text parts of that turn only (A2's view-model rows: no receipts, tool lines, cards or retracted narration), passed through toSpeakable (markdown stripped even when spokenMode is on), queued sentence by sentence as the text streams (so Auto starts speaking before the turn ends). Voice: the phone's own (iOS: every AVSpeechSynthesisVoice is on the device, Enhanced first; Android: a voice whose name says 'local' and never one that says 'network', Google TTS's naming; none → the engine's default for the language). iOS speaks with useApplicationAudioSession: false (the system manages speech's own audio session after recognition left the session in playAndRecord/measurement; owner check OT-V3). A turn with cards or receipts also shows 'See it in the chat' (routes.chat(id)).

Quick-ask shows AND speaks the AI notice ONCE, before the first spoken reply of a voice session ('Hi, this is Auto, your AI assistant.', the server's own words: orchestrator/modules/policy/ai_disclosure.py VOICE_GREETING), with the answering agent's name when it is not Auto. No ten-minute reminder, no repeat within a session (D73, Gerard 23 Oct: the AI label is one small muted caption, never a pill and never a lock; the voice notice is spoken once per session). A session starts at the first quick-ask after the voice screen mounts and ends when it unmounts or the app goes to the background. Auto Live adds nothing spoken: the server speaks its greeting in the call.

One pure reducer (src/voice/machine/voice-reducer.ts) drives the voice screen for quick-ask and, in phase 2, Live: phases idle | listening | thinking | speaking | error; micOpen separately (the capture truth); the view-model derives every word on screen from it. Hooks feed it events and run its effects; nothing else holds voice state.
decisions.source: lead brief (the voice screen states driven by one reducer)

decisions.text: voiceDress(resolvedStyle) paints A5's core: Studio (and an installed theme, which uses the Studio layout) → the rings' structure (outer ring, ticks, dashed ring, crosshair) in --foreground (ink) and their motion (arcs, segments, pulse) in --accent (orange), no HUD overlay, Auto only when the theme brings a mascot; Play → the look's accent for both with Auto (A5's Mascot) in the centre always; HUD → hud.accent for both, its overlay, Auto when the look's auto is 'on'. Colours from the resolved style only. motion = resolved.motion.loops (Reduce Motion, HUD's motion off).

AppState 'background' (including the screen locking) → abort listening (nothing sent), stop speech, end the AI-notice session and (phase 2) leave Live. iOS 'inactive' (Control Centre, an incoming-call banner) does nothing by itself; the audio-session interruption that a real call, Siri or an alarm causes reaches the app as the recognizer's 'interrupted' error → abort, keep the words heard on screen un-sent, 'Interrupted. Hold to talk when you're ready.' A route change the module cannot recover (a headset or Bluetooth device going away) → abort with 'The microphone changed. Hold to talk again.' Coming back to 'active' never reopens the mic, resumes speech or rejoins Live by itself.
decisions.source: decision 33, PRD-001 §4.9 (the mic never opens without a press); expo-speech-recognition ios/ExpoSpeechRecognizer.swift:720-775

decisions.text: Decision (a): Auto Live ENDS — and quick-ask aborts — when the app leaves the screen, on Android and iOS alike, and the copy says so on return ('Auto Live ended when Automatos Go left the screen.'). Option (b), unblocking FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE with a Play declaration, is not taken: (1) Gerard decided it (decision 33: 'No background microphone, no Android microphone foreground service'); (2) it is a native change (app.json → a new fingerprint and an iOS build from the shared quota, D43) in a wave that ships over the air; (3) iOS has no UIBackgroundModes 'audio' either (foundation K11), so a background call would differ by platform; (4) the module evidence: @livekit/react-native-expo-plugin 1.1.0 adds NO permission (its android/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml is empty; its plugin only adds the livekit/podspecs Podfile source, the android.audioType meta-data and an optional screen-share-service flag that needs FOREGROUND_SERVICE + FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PROJECTION); FOREGROUND_SERVICE comes from @livekit/react-native's own library manifest and its only service is @livekit/react-native-webrtc's MediaProjectionService (foregroundServiceType mediaProjection, screen share), which the app never starts; no installed module declares FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MICROPHONE. Android 14 also stops a backgrounded app's microphone without a microphone-type foreground service started in the foreground, so ending the call is the honest behaviour, not a degraded one. The screen stays on while voice is active (KV12) so a hands-free call does not end by itself. Revisit only if Gerard reverses decision 33.
decisions.source: coordinator question 21 Oct; decision 33; app.json blockedPermissions; docs/native-modules.md 'Blocked' FOREGROUND_SERVICE row

decisions.text: The screen stays on while the mic is open, a reply is being spoken or a Live call is up (expo-keep-awake activateKeepAwakeAsync / deactivateKeepAwake with one tag, in src/voice/interruptions/keep-awake.ts only), and is released otherwise. expo-keep-awake is a dependency of expo 54 (~15.0.8 in node_modules/expo/package.json), autolinked into the foundation's binary: import it, never add it to package.json. If typecheck or lint refuses the import, write 'FOUNDATION GAP: expo-keep-awake not a direct dependency' and keep the rest of the story.

One audio owner at a time: none | recognizer | speaker | live. Claiming the recognizer stops the speaker (barge-in); Live takes the audio from both (aborts recognition, stops speech); quick-ask is disabled while Live is up.

The Live button shows only when: canVoiceLive(discovery) AND the bootstrap's ai_providers is a list that names id 'retell' (W3 US-017b lists Retell exactly when the workspace can use Auto Live — platform switch, Retell armed, the workspace's switch and, on SaaS, the plan; so a Basic or Pro SaaS workspace never sees it, and a self-hosted install sees it once its operator armed Retell) AND roleCan(role, 'chat'). ai_providers absent (a server before W3) or null → hidden. A refusal at the mint is still handled: a 403 whose detail names a plan, tier, Business, upgrade, credit or price shows the fixed 'Auto Live isn't available for this workspace. Ask your workspace owner.' (D8); every other refusal detail is a user-facing sentence and is shown as written (PRD-001 US-020); 502 'Auto Live couldn't start the call. Try again.'. Local edition: the same gate, no plan words ever.
decisions.source: decision 34, D8, PRD-001 US-020 AC3, W1 US-008a, W3 US-017b

decisions.text: Only src/voice/live/livekit-session.ts imports @livekit/react-native and livekit-client; it calls registerGlobals() once, lazily, before the first Room (app/_layout.tsx is not this kit's; if the device check OT-V9 shows LiveKit needs it at app start, that is a FOUNDATION GAP for the lead). Only src/voice/quick-ask/recognizer.ts and src/voice/permissions/permissions.ts import expo-speech-recognition; only src/voice/speech/speaker.ts imports expo-speech; only src/voice/interruptions/keep-awake.ts imports expo-keep-awake (gate-enforced).

v1 joins over LiveKit only: the mint's transport absent or 'livekit'. 'gateway' (Retell's WHIP-style signalling since SDK 3.0.0) or anything else → no join, 'Auto Live can't connect from this phone yet. Hold to talk still works.', logged without the token. A native gateway client is possible on @livekit/react-native-webrtc's RTCPeerConnection (retellLiveKitProtocol.gatewayForTheRecord) but is an open question for the lead, not this wave.

The voice screen is app/(app)/voice.tsx at '/voice' (optionally '/voice?chat=<id>'); the path and its builder live in src/voice/nav.ts (VOICE_SCREENS, voiceRoute) — src/navigation/routes.ts is never edited (the foundation owns it and the connect kit edits it). Every other destination uses the foundation's builders (routes.chat, routes.cc.board, routes.settings) and A5's src/styles/nav.ts.

No copy says 'nothing leaves your server' or anything as broad (never leaves, no data is sent, 100% local, fully private, stays entirely on). Quick-ask's copy may say the voice recognition runs on the phone (true by KV4); the words still go to Auto's AI providers as any chat does (the consent sheet names them). Live's copy says the voice goes to Retell: 'Auto Live sends your voice to Retell while the call is on.' Gate-enforced on added lines.

Consent for Retell is the shell's (connect KC11: the sheet names every ai_providers entry, Retell included, and asks again when the list changes). Before a mint, Live reads the connect kit's consent record read-only (src/consent/policy.ts consentNeeded or its equivalent — RE-VERIFY after connect): when the record does not cover the current list, no mint, the copy 'Auto Live sends your voice to Retell, an AI voice service. Agree to the updated list of AI providers first.' and the connect kit's way back to its consent step (its exported hook; none exported → FOUNDATION GAP and the copy alone). This kit builds no second consent sheet.

userStories.description: As a user, I want my voice turned into words on my phone, never on Apple's or Google's servers (KV4, decision 32), and a plain reason when my phone cannot do it.
acceptanceCriteria: src/voice/quick-ask/recognition-policy.ts (pure): recognitionPolicy({platform 'ios' | 'android', androidApiLevel?, supportsOnDevice, recognitionAvailable, locale, supportedLocales?, installedLocales?}) → {kind 'ready', options} | {kind 'download', locale} | {kind 'unavailable', reason 'no-on-device' | 'android-too-old' | 'language-missing' | 'no-recognizer'}: iOS ready only when supportsOnDevice; Android ready only when androidApiLevel >= 33 AND supportsOnDevice AND the locale (or its language, 'en' for 'en-GB') is in installedLocales; supported but not installed → 'download'; anything else → unavailable → DONE — recognition-policy.ts recognitionPolicy() as specified (Android also ready when on-device works but isRecognitionAvailable is false; iOS also needs an available recognizer, as the module refuses otherwise, ExpoSpeechRecognizer.swift:216); recognition-policy.test.ts

userStories.title: iOS: a release, tap or STOP sent while recognition is still starting leaves the mic open (KV5)
userStories.description: Review finding (HIGH; KV5, D-SCREEN-ON). On iOS, expo-speech-recognition 3.1.3 starts recognition inside a Swift Task that awaits several steps before capture begins (node_modules/expo-speech-recognition/ios/ExpoSpeechRecognitionModule.swift:174-260: getLocale, the recognizer's creation on the first hold, hasPermissionToRecord, then ExpoSpeechRecognizer.start → startRecognizer, which sends 'start' and 'audiostart': ExpoSpeechRecognizer.swift:200-256), while stop() and abort() run in Tasks of their own (ExpoSpeechRecognitionModule.swift:360-379): with no recognizer yet they send 'end' at once, and with one whose task has not started they reset and send 'end' (ExpoSpeechRecognizer.swift:154-176). A stop or abort that lands in that window is answered with an 'end', and the capture then starts anyway. The app does not recover: src/voice/quick-ask/recognizer-core.ts:130-133 drops any 'end' while the session is 'starting' as the previous session's, and nothing re-sends the stop or abort when that session's 'start'/'audiostart' then arrives (recognizer-core.ts:234-251). (1) A tap released after listen() called recognizer.start (src/voice/quick-ask/quick-ask-hold.ts:63-74 and 143-146) ends the hold and gives the audio back, so the capture that then opens (MIC LIVE on) cannot be closed by STOP, by leaving the screen or by the background: abortListening aborts only while a hold exists or the recognizer owns the audio (src/voice/quick-ask/quick-ask-store.ts:145-149, called from quick-ask-engine.ts:66-79 and quick-ask-interrupt.ts:25-28), and both are already cleared. Only the next press ends it. (2) A release at HOLD_MIN_MS or later inside the window cancels the HOLD_MAX_MS timer (quick-ask-hold.ts:139) and sends stop(). Its 'end' is dropped, the capture opens with no timer, and the hold stays set, so every later press returns at quick-ask-hold.ts:122 until STOP. (3) A STOP or a background inside the window ends the hold the same way as (1). Android is not affected (start and stop are posted in order to one main-thread Handler: android/.../ExpoSpeechService.kt:116-205), but the fix must hold there too. The window is narrowest after the first hold; the first hold after launch (recognizer creation) and a quick tap are the likely triggers. The device re-check (a quick tap and a quick STOP on the first hold after launch) is the owner's, with OT-V4.
acceptanceCriteria: Cause: recognizer-core.ts drops an 'end' while the session is 'starting' and never re-sends a stop() or abort() asked for in that state; abortListening (quick-ask-store.ts:145-149) does not abort a capture the reducer knows is open once the hold and the audio owner are cleared; after a release, nothing bounds a stop whose 'end' never comes (the HOLD_MAX_MS timer is cancelled at quick-ask-hold.ts:139)

Change (recognizer-core.ts): the session remembers a stop() or abort() asked for while it is 'starting' (abort wins over stop), and when that session's first 'start' or 'audiostart' arrives it sends that call to the port again, once. An aborted session's words still say nothing; a stopped session still says its final once, at its real end. Nothing in this path calls port.start, and the on-device options are unchanged (KV4)

Change (quick-ask-store.ts and its callers in quick-ask-engine.ts and quick-ask-interrupt.ts): abortListening also aborts while the reducer's micOpen is true (the capture truth, KV5), so STOP, unmount, 'covered' and 'background' always close a capture the app has seen open, with or without a hold

Change (quick-ask-hold.ts, config.ts): after a release's recognizer.stop(), a bounded settle timer (a named constant in config.ts, e.g. RELEASE_SETTLE_MS) aborts the recognizer and ends the hold if the hold is still set when it fires (nothing sent; the reducer's nothing_heard). The timer is cancelled when the hold ends normally, and HOLD TO TALK is never left dead after a release

Tests (src/voice/__tests__/recognizer-session.test.ts over recognizer-port.ts): stop() and, separately, abort() while 'starting', each followed by an 'end' (dropped) then 'start' + 'audiostart' → the port's stop or abort is called again exactly once; the aborted session says no final; the stopped one says its final once at the real end; a stale 'end' before a fresh session's first event with no stop asked is still dropped
